title: Odisha Artificial Intelligence Policy-2025
issuing_body: Electronics & Information Technology (E&IT) Department, Government of Odisha

timeline.event: Initial AI strategy presentation to Chief Secretary
Brainstorming workshop with MeitY, industry and academia on state AI strategy
State Cabinet (20th meeting) approves the policy; Parliamentary Affairs Dept memo 3971 dated 29.05.2025
E&IT Department Resolution No. 3227/E&IT issued; gazette publication ordered
Operational Guidelines for the policy issued (per IMPRI; press reported roadmap 19-20 March 2026)

summary: State AI policy adopted by Cabinet and issued as an E&IT Department resolution. It sets five-year and 2036 targets on compute, skilling, schooling, energy and ethics, and creates an Odisha AI Mission with an AI Taskforce and an AI Cell at OCAC.
key_provisions: Four strategy pillars: infrastructure, skills, energy, policy; in operation for 5 years from gazette notification or until superseded
Odisha AI Mission with two layers: an AI Taskforce chaired by the Principal Secretary, E&IT, and an AI Cell under OCAC (Technical Directorate of E&IT)
Compute: state data centre of 5 MW to be doubled by 2029; use of IndiaAI Compute portal and AI Kosh datasets; Odia-language LLM development prioritised
Skilling: 8,000 people per year trained in AI by 2029 (10% of national Srijan/YuvAI target); 75% of state government officials trained by 2029 and 100% by 2036
Schooling: 35% of schools to have an AI curriculum by 2029 and 90% by 2036; seven AI innovation centres in Bhubaneswar institutions by 2036
Energy: 50% renewable share for AI infrastructure by 2029-30 and 65% by 2036; ethical-use guidelines on bias, privacy, transparency and accountability to be developed
Budget 2025-26 allocated Rs 20 crore to the Odisha AI Mission (reported by IMPRI)
confidence_note: Official resolution PDF (scanned, OCR noisy) read; resolution number 3227/E&IT and memos dated 18.06.2025 visible; cabinet date 28.05.2025 from press and the resolution's reference to Parliamentary Affairs memo of 29.05.2025. The brief's 'Sept 2025' approval date is not supported. Rs 20 crore budget figure is from IMPRI, not the PDF.

AI labs at IIT Bhubaneswar, NIT Rourkela, IIIT Bhubaneswar and NISER for research and skilling
Centre of Excellence on a hub-and-spoke model linking government, academia, industry and startups, with quarterly evaluations
State Open AI Hub as a repository for open-source tools, datasets and models; micro-grants for open-source contributors and pilot funding for innovation-challenge winners
Priority sectors: agriculture, healthcare, disaster management and public service delivery; sovereign AI hub projected to create 5,000 jobs
confidence_note: Official guidelines document not located online; contents from two trade/press reports and IMPRI. Date conflict: press coverage on 19-20 March 2026 versus IMPRI's '30 March 2026' date, so month precision used.
